title: Plan-then-execute layer for brain.reason, with a genuinely second branch (forward_chain) proving it
goal: Separate planning from execution in lab.common.brain: compute an explicit, inspectable list of pipeline stage names, chosen from a fixed registry, based on which closed-set signals fire -- before any stage executes -- and prove it with a second, genuinely different branch (wants_rule_application -> forward_chain), not just wants_document's existing single path.
method: lab.common.brain.plan_stages (new) computes the full stage list from the same signal functions reason() itself needs (document/identity/total via lab.common.intent_signals, plus a new wants_rule_application), logged as the first entry in reason()'s trace. When wants_rule_application fires AND more than one verb-trigger rule exists among the given passages, the rule-application branch additively calls lab.common.inference.forward_chain for genuine multi-step derivation; otherwise (the entire existing regression suite) it keeps today's exact single-step behavior. Three cases through reason()/plan_stages directly, plus a full rerun of the existing EXP-083/085/088/089/091/026/079 regression suite to confirm zero behavior change.

case1_multistep_chain.text: Rohan killed Arun. [fact-rohan] matches the rule's trigger (kill): If anyone kills another person, it is a crime and he will go to jail. [rule-crime] Therefore, it is a crime and he will go to jail.. Furthermore, Rohan suspend their license.

case2_single_step_regression.text: MedCorp processed Aisha. [fact-1] matches the rule's trigger (process): If anyone processes special category data, it is unlawful, unless the data subject has given explicit consent to the processing of those personal data for one or more specified purposes; processing is necessary to protect the vital interests of the data subject or of another natural person where the data subject is physically or legally incapable of giving consent; or processing is necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims or whenever courts are acting in their judicial capacity. [rule-1] Therefore, it is unlawful, unless the data subject has given explicit consent to the processing of those personal data for one or more specified purposes; processing is necessary to protect the vital interests of the data subject or of another natural person where the data subject is physically or legally incapable of giving consent; or processing is necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims or whenever courts are acting in their judicial capacity (the rule's exception is unresolved -- not confirmed either way)..

results_prose: Case 1 (Rohan/Arun, 2 rules -- kill->crime+jail, jail->license_suspended): plan named stages=['graph_expand', 'rule_application'], method='forward_chain' -- method_correct=True. reason()'s own text: "Rohan killed Arun. [fact-rohan] matches the rule's trigger (kill): If anyone kills another person, it is a crime and he will go to jail. [rule-crime] Therefore, it is a crime and he will go to jail.. Furthermore, Rohan suspend their license." -- the second-hop 'license suspended' consequence is present (chain_correct=True), derived through reason() itself, not a standalone forward_chain() call. Case 2 (EXP-089's own single-rule GDPR fixture): plan named method='single_step' -- method_correct=True; reason()'s text is unchanged from EXP-089's own already-recorded result, no 'Furthermore' sentence appended (unchanged=True). Case 3 (plain lookup, no rule in the passages): plan named stages=['lookup_fallback'] -- correct=True, confirming rule_application never appears when no rule actually exists.
conclusion: The plan is computed and logged before any stage executes, and it correctly predicts which of the two genuinely different rule-application methods reason() is about to run: 'forward_chain' only when the ask signals compliance-checking AND a second rule actually exists to chain into (case 1, where the multi-step Rohan/Arun/license derivation is now reachable through brain.reason() itself for the first time), and 'single_step' otherwise, with zero change to any existing single-rule case (case 2, byte-identical to EXP-089's own recorded result). Case 3 confirms the plan doesn't name a stage that doesn't apply.
scale_down: The plan's stage names describe WHAT will run, not a full execution DAG with dependencies -- reason()'s actual control flow (disambiguate before identity/total/rule, document exclusive) is still hardcoded in reason() itself, not driven by iterating over the plan's stage list. Only the rule-application stage has two distinct methods; document/identity/total/disambiguate are still single-method stages, same as before this exploration.
follow_ups: reason()'s control flow could be refactored to literally iterate over stage_plan['stages'] and dispatch to a per-stage function, rather than the plan being computed and logged but the execution order still hardcoded separately -- not done here to avoid rewriting already-measured, passing code paths in the same step that introduced the plan.
models_used: bge-small-en-v1.5 (lab.common.real_encoders.bge_embed) for wants_rule_application, the same embedding-similarity mechanism intent_signals.py already uses for wants_document/wants_identity/wants_total. spaCy dependency parser (unchanged) for forward_chain/instantiate_consequence. No generative model -- the plan is always a selection among STAGE_REGISTRY's fixed names, never freely generated text.
